title: Staggered client-cohort release scratchpad
body:
Purpose and quick context:
- Notes for running a slow, staggered cohort-based rollout for model/runtime changes where we need fine-grained traffic shaping and early detection without relying on a single large canary.
- Target: reduce blast radius while getting representative production signals (different client types, session lengths, and geographic spread).
- Not a formal runbook — personal scratchpad to iterate on thresholds and monitoring queries.

High-level strategy:
1) Identify 4 client cohorts by traffic characteristic: small-burst clients (mobile push), mid-size interactive (web chat), long-session (editor/autocomplete), bg-batch (embeddings/ingestion).
2) Deploy new version behind a feature-flagged routing rule; route cohorts sequentially with hold windows for observation.
3) Keep default fallback to last-known-good for any cohort that breaches thresholds.

Timing and ramp windows (UTC):
- T0 (deploy to infra, no traffic): immediate after build pass. Smoke tests for 15m.
- T+30m: Cohort A (small-burst) -> 1% traffic for 30m.
- T+90m: Cohort A -> 5% for 45m.
- T+3h: Cohort B (mid-size interactive) -> 1% for 30m.
- T+4h: Cohort A -> 10%, Cohort B -> 5% for 1h.
- T+8h: Cohort C (long-session) -> 1% for 1h (synthetic session probes running).
- T+12h: Gradual ramp to 50% over next 24h depending on signals.
Notes: adjust windows at night/weekend conservatively; prefer slower ramps for major infra changes.

Acceptance signals (must be green to proceed):
- Client-facing SLA metrics (rolling 5m): p95 latency delta < +25% vs baseline AND p50 delta < +10%.
- Error rate: 5xx rate < 0.3% absolute and < 2x relative increase vs baseline for a 30m window.
- Latency tail spike rule: no sustained p99 increase > 2x baseline for > 15m.
- Business/key transaction success (e.g., generation complete): success rate >= 99.0% for cohort.
- Cost/throughput sanity: token/sec / GPU utilization within expected band for the model profile.

Primary rollback triggers (if any one holds for defined window):
- Immediate rollback: 5xx > 1.5% for two consecutive 5m buckets OR any client-facing data corruption incident.
- Fast rollback: sustained error rate > 0.5% for 30m AND other signals (p95 latency +50% and user complaints).
- Pause-and-investigate: metric drift (error or latency) > threshold for one cohort but isolated to that cohort; keep rollout paused and route cohort back to previous version while investigating.

Investigation checklist when a trigger fires:
- Tag incident as "staged-rollout" and ping #releases and oncall SRE.
- Capture quick diffs: git rev, model hash, build artifacts, infra versions.
- Run targeted smoke requests against both old and new endpoints with identical payloads (use synthetic tokens and stored prompt set).
- Check KV cache hit rates and KV warming logs (long-session cohorts often hit cache skew issues).
- Confirm no upstream dependency version drift (tokenizer, tokenizer-service, storage).
- If rollback needed: execute traffic-pin command and wait 3m for steady state, then scale down new variant.

Communications and escalation:
- Immediate: @channel #releases with brief status and action (rollback/pause).
- Paging: if rollback fails or incident escalates, call SRE oncall and product PM.
- Postmortem: if rollback or any customer-impacting incident, start a postmortem in Confluence within 48h and link INF ticket.

Synthetic and probing plan (make these run automatically):
- Lightweight synthetic suite per cohort (5 request types) running every 1m for A/B endpoints. Record latency, success, log traces.
- Long-session probe: create a 30m synthetic session that tests cache warmup and KV reuse.
- Background probes: bulk embed workloads run once per hour to validate throughput/backpressure.

Prometheus/Telemetry sample queries (placeholder, tweak for dashboards):
- error_rate_5xx_cohort = sum(rate(http_responses_total{status=~"5..",cohort=~".*"}[5m])) / sum(rate(http_requests_total{cohort=~".*"}[5m]))
- p95_latency = histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, cohort))
- token_throughput = sum(rate(tokens_generated_total[1m])) by (cohort)
(plug these into per-cohort dashboards for gating).

Quick ops commands (examples, adapt to infra):
- route 1% of traffic to new: curl -X POST $ROUTER/api/traffic -d '{"cohort":"A","variant":"new","percent":1}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
- pin back to previous: ./infra/bin/traffic-pin --cohort A --variant old --reason "rollback: errors"
- fetch traces for request id: go run ./tools/fetchtraces -id <trace_id> -env prod

Data collection to save for postmortem (capture as artifacts):
- example request/response pairs (redact PII) for failed requests.
- flamegraphs at time of incident for affected hosts.
- GPU metrics (util, memory, power) and scheduling backlogs.

Known risk areas / hypotheses to watch for:
- Client cohort mismatch: small clients may not expose long-tail KV issues seen in long-session cohort.
- Tokenizer or preprocessor changes cause silent failures on rare inputs — monitor failed-parse metrics.
- Autoscaler spin-up latency when new variant hits a burst — observe queue lengths during ramp.

To-dos / follow-ups before next run:
- Add a dedicated dashboard tile that overlays cohort A vs cohort B p95 in same chart.
- Add synthetic probe that mimics a 10k-token streaming session (long_session probe).
- File a tech debt ticket to add automatic rollback automation for specific thresholds (INF-4390).
- Coordinate with Release QA to expand sample prompt set by 30% for long-session tests.

Loose notes and thoughts (brain-dump):
- Consider an "early-warn" metric that combines tiny increases across latency, error, and trace duration into a single score — easier to gate on correlated small degradations.
- For big infra changes (scheduler/kernel upgrades) prefer cohort assignment by region to isolate infra variability.
- If we see cohort-specific regressions repeatedly, add a simple client signature header and persist last-known-good variant per client id for quick pinback.

End of scratchpad. Keep iterating thresholds after each roll (document what changed and why).
